evidence.quote: Starting next month, we will be purchasing $55 billion of securities per month, down $10 billion per month from our current rate.
it probably means something on the order of around six months or that type of thing.
These conditions warrant the continuation of highly accommodative policy reflected in today’s policy statement.
we are fully committed to the 2 percent inflation objective, and we do not want to undershoot inflation for a prolonged period of time.
In contrast, labor market conditions have continued to improve.
the Committee will likely continue to reduce the pace of asset purchases in measured steps at future meetings.

parsed.rationale: The Chair announces continued tapering and suggests purchases end next fall, with rate hikes possibly about six months later, but she emphasizes highly accommodative policy, below-target inflation, substantial slack and rates below normal for some time. On net the signal is a mild dovish lean.
